Scavenger receptor (SR) family
The scavenger receptors belong to a large family of pattern recognition receptors, which can interact with a wide range of ligands.
Interacting with the circulating native or modiﬁed lipoproteins, such as oxLDL, these receptors modulate vascular inﬂammation,
lipid accumulation, and plaque formation. Two important SR, CD36 and SR-BI, play a role in atherogenesis in different ways.

B1, a high-afﬁnity HDL receptor mediates the uptake of HDL cholesterol ester into the liver. SR-BI also facilitates the bidirectional
ﬂux of free cholesterol (FC) between cells and HDL. Also, hepatic SR-BI has been linked to clearance of proatherogenic lipoproteins
VLDL and Lp(a). Thus, hepatic SR-BI is thought to protect against atherosclerosis by promoting RCT and maintaining anti-
atherogenic characteristics of HDL and decreasing atherogenic lipoproteins. Lastly, there is compelling evidence in support of athe-
roprotective functions of macrophage SR-BI.
